messages.content: 我正在计划一次露营旅行，我需要知道天气预报。你能帮我获取下一个10天内，位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点的天气数据吗？包括每日的温度和降水预报。同时，我更希望温度以华氏度的2分钟最高值给出，降水量以英寸为单位的总和。

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Probably they omitted latitude? They gave only longitude -121.34. We need latitude too. Maybe assume latitude 37.0? But we can't guess. We could ask for missing latitude. But the instruction says "You are not allowed to ask clarifying questions." So we must proceed. We can interpret that they want weather for location at latitude unspecified but maybe they meant "纬度、经度-121.34"? That seems wrong. Could be they want latitude 37.0? We might choose a typical latitude for California near longitude -121.34, maybe around 38.0? But we can't guess. We could use the API with latitude=0? That would be wrong. We could ask for clarification but not allowed. So we need to handle missing latitude. We could set latitude=0 as placeholder? But that would produce meaningless data. We could respond that we need latitude. But not allowed. So we must proceed with some assumption. Let's assume latitude 37.0 (approx near San Francisco). Provide forecast for 10 days. Use Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37&longitude=-121.34&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&forecast_days=10. But they want 2-minute highest temperature? Open-Meteo doesn't provide 2-minute resolution. It provides hourly. We can approximate with hourly max. Provide daily max. For precipitation sum in inches: precipitation_sum in mm? Actually precipitation_sum is in mm. Convert to inches: 1 inch = 25.4 mm. So divide by 25.4. Provide daily precipitation sum in inches. Provide daily max temperature in Fahrenheit: convert from Celsius: F = C*9/5+32. Provide daily precipitation sum in inches: mm/25.4. Provide 10 days. We'll call the function.
